claim: To use Firewall Manager you must enable AWS Config, for each member account (including the administrator account) and each Region that has resources to protect; AWS Config charges apply.
question: Which service must be enabled in every member account for Firewall Manager to work?

values.display: To use Firewall Manager, you must enable AWS Config.

evidence.quote: To use Firewall Manager, you must enable AWS Config.
You incur charges for your AWS Config settings, according to AWS Config pricing.

claim: For every Firewall Manager policy you can choose to only view the accounts and resources that are out of compliance without taking corrective action, or to automatically remediate noncompliant resources.
question: Can a Firewall Manager policy report noncompliance without changing resources?

evidence.quote: You can choose to view the accounts and resources that are out of compliance without taking corrective action or to automatically remediate noncompliant resources.

claim: Resource tags can also define Firewall Manager policy scope: you can include or exclude resources that have all of the tags in a list, or apply the policy only to resources that have any of the specified tags.
question: Can resource tags decide which resources a Firewall Manager policy protects?

values.display: Resource tags can also be used to define policy scope.

evidence.quote: Resource tags can also be used to define policy scope. You can choose to apply a policy by excluding or including resources that have all of the tags in a list. Alternatively, you can choose to apply a policy only to resources that have any of a specified tag in a list.

claim: You can apply a Firewall Manager policy to all accounts in the organization, to only a list of included accounts and OUs, or to all except a list of excluded accounts and OUs.
question: How do you limit a Firewall Manager policy to some OUs?

values.display: a specific list of included account numbers
To all except a specific list of excluded account numbers

evidence.quote: To only a specific list of included account numbers and AWS Organizations organizational units (OUs)
To all except a specific list of excluded account numbers and AWS Organizations organizational units (OUs)

claim: A Firewall Manager AWS WAF policy can create and manage new web ACLs for in-scope resources, replacing web ACLs already in use, or keep the web ACLs already associated with in-scope resources and retrofit them for use by the policy.
question: Must a Firewall Manager AWS WAF policy replace web ACLs that accounts already use?

values.display: replacing any web ACLs that are already in use
retrofit them for use by the policy

evidence.quote: You can configure the policy to create and manage all new web ACLs for in-scope resources, replacing any web ACLs that are already in use. Alternately, you can configure the policy to keep any web ACLs that are already associated with in-scope resources, and retrofit them for use by the policy.

note: d068. The retrofit date belongs to the numbers+changes lens.

claim: Firewall Manager can have one or multiple administrators; with multiple administrators you apply administrative scope conditions to each, such as the accounts or OUs, Regions and policy types it can manage.
question: Can different teams each administer part of Firewall Manager?

values.display: you can have one or multiple administrators
apply administrative scope conditions to each administrator

evidence.quote: With AWS Firewall Manager you can have one or multiple administrators who can manage the firewall resources of your organization. If you want to use multiple Firewall Manager administrators in your organization, you can apply administrative scope conditions to each administrator to define the resources that they can manage.

note: d071. The launch date of multiple administrators belongs to the numbers+changes lens.
